regime: Choppy Fade (NQ Popped PCE Then Faded, ES Red, Gold Reversed)
summary: August PCE printed cooler than expected, the tape popped, then gave it back all day. The Nasdaq ran to 30,906 at the open and faded to close 30,726, up just 0.25 percent and well off the high but still above its rising stop. The S&P could not hold the bid, closing down 0.22 percent under a falling stop, so the split between tech and the broad market is still here. Gold was the big reversal, tagging 4,216 overnight then dumping to close 4,149.8 as its stop flipped down, while crude bounced 1.52 percent to reclaim its stop above 90 and the VIX ticked up to 16.34 into quarter-end.

event.name: August PCE + Q2 GDP (third estimate)
event.actual: Headline 3.4% YoY, core 3.0% YoY (+0.2% MoM), spending +0.9%
event.surprise: Cooler than expected on both headline and core
event.nqReaction: NQ popped to a 30,906 high at the open, then faded all session to close +0.25% well off the high.
event.crossAsset: Gold reversed lower (-0.82%), crude bounced (+1.52%), ES lagged red (-0.22%); the VIX ticked up to 16.34.

observe.name: OBSERVE lane
observe.note: No OBSERVE-lane signals today. OBSERVE candidates such as GAP_NQ and TSMOM252LO_NQ sit outside the Net Alpha Pro curriculum and are tracked for research only.

risk.note: Throttle stays REDUCED. The PCE event cleared without a volatility spike, but the tape gave a split, low-conviction read: NQ faded from its high, ES closed red below its stop and gold reversed hard. That is not a clean trend to lean into. Thursday brings jobless claims and ISM Manufacturing and Friday brings the jobs report, so keep size measured and let a real trend confirm. Most prop firms restrict trading around major scheduled releases, so check your firm's news rule before the claims and ISM prints.

psychology: Cooler inflation, a green screen at the open, then a slow bleed all day. That sequence traps anyone who chases the first move. The number was good, buyers showed up, and the market handed most of it back into the close. The reaction to news tells you more than the news itself. When price cannot hold a move built on a favorable headline, that is real information, and today it said the buyers were not committed. Grade yourself on your patience while the tape proved itself. Calling the print was never the job.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN (MNQ)
fullReport.html: Opening range high 30,810.25, low 30,682.25, width 128 points (about 0.42%). Break UP at 13:45 UTC to a 30,906 high, then price faded all the way back inside the range and below the 30,829.51 NYVWAP, closing 30,726 inside the opening range. No clean playbook entry confirmed, but this was textbook Back-in-Range habitat: an up-break that makes a new high then closes back inside the range. Filter state (Wednesday): no CPI, no FOMC. Hand-off and Midrange are off on Wednesdays; Back-in-Range and Bounce were eligible. Lesson: on an event morning, wait for acceptance before trusting the first push.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout (Regime Filter)
fullReport.html: No signal fired. ROC(12) +0.35% over the last twelve hours, weak momentum despite the higher close. Price closed 30,726, above the 50-EMA near 30,679, so the regime filter is not blocking and E3v2 stays borderline rather than off. Relative volume is disclaimed on a continuous contract. The breakout long stays parked until a real volume and momentum thrust shows above the 50-EMA.

fullReport.title: AVWAP Deviation Band Reversal (MNQ)
fullReport.html: AVWAP center 30,809 (1 sigma about 56 points). Bands: plus 2 sigma 30,921, plus 3 sigma 30,977; minus 2 sigma 30,696, minus 3 sigma 30,640. Price closed 30,726, between the minus 1 sigma (30,753) and minus 2 sigma (30,696) bands, mild lower extension after the fade. No minus 2 or minus 3 sigma exhaustion tag, so there is no reversion fade yet. Watch a tag of minus 2 sigma near 30,696 for a mean-reversion setup, or a reclaim of AVWAP for the bounce.
